thread:
maria: Heads-up — product asked for a dashboard that ties request-id propagation to sampled traces and per-route SLOs. Need input on what runtime fields we can reliably expose without blowing ingest costs.

kevin: +1. Are we talking about full traces or just a sampled flag and span count per request id?

maria: Ideally both, but start minimal: expose `req_id`, `trace_sampled` (bool), `span_count`, `route`, `model_variant`, `latency_ms`. Then dashboards can join sampled traces to telemetry for quality checks.

ashley: Is `req_id` generated at the edge or can callers supply their own? We should normalize both `x-request-id` and `x-redwood-req-id`.

oliver: Runtime currently accepts caller-provided `x-request-id` and falls back to `generated_req_id`. We can add a normalized header `x-rw-req-id` in logs + metrics.

ben: Important: when a request fans out (tool calls, background tasks), we need parent/child span ids in logs so the dashboard can correlate. But that means more metadata per log line. Cost risk.

maria: Agreed on cost. Proposal: for non-sampled requests emit only `req_id`, `route`, `latency_ms`, `sampled=false` as a lightweight metric point. For sampled requests emit a richer event including `span_count` and `trace_id`. That way trace storage is bounded by sample rate.

kevin: How will sampling be controlled? Per-route percent? Global policy? Product wants to increase sampling on failing routes.

ashley: We already have a runtime flag `trace.sample_rate` but it's global. Could extend to `trace.sample_rate[route]` and allow runtime to override via a small control API.

oliver: Technical caveat: when we override sample rate mid-request (e.g., canary rollout triggers higher sampling), we must ensure the tracer can mark the trace as sampled and downstream nodes honor it. Need header `x-rw-sampled:1`.

ben: Also add `x-rw-force-sample` for debug captures — admin-only and rate-limited. That will help SRE reproduce issues without changing global rate.

sam_oncall: From oncall POV, we need a cheap signal in metrics to alert on high error rate per `req_id` cohort. Example: `errors_by_reqid_sampled=0/1` plus `err_rate_p95`.

maria: Dashboard UX: show heatmap of routes vs sample_rate, and a toggle to overlay sampled traces. Add a quick query: `count(requests) by route, sample_flag` and `avg(latency_ms) by route, sample_flag`.

kevin: Implementation checklist from runtime: 1) emit normalized header name, 2) emit lightweight metric point for every request with `req_id` and `sampled` flag, 3) for sampled traces include `trace_id` and `span_count` to trace-ingest.

ashley: Thoughts on metric names? Suggest `requests.count`, `requests.latency_ms.p95`, `requests.span_count.sampled`. Keep tags: `route`, `model`, `env`, `customer_tier`.

oliver: Also add `request.propagation.missing:bool` so dashboards can show how often callers drop req ids. Right now some SDKs strip headers.

ben: Logging example we can standardize on: ```
{"timestamp":"...","x-rw-req-id":"abc123","trace_id":"t-zzz","sampled":true,"span_count":4,"route":"/v1/generate","latency_ms":132}
```

maria: Ops question — where do we store the lightweight request rows? Metrics backend (Prom/OTLP) or logs-based index? Metrics is cheaper for aggregation; logs for joining with trace payloads.

sam_oncall: Use metrics for the 1-per-request signals and only write sampled traces to our trace store. Alerts run on metrics. Dashboards can link to traces when sampled.

kevin: OK. I'll add a runtime API PR that exposes `GET /internal/trace-config` and `POST /internal/trace-config` (admin-only) to change per-route sample rates. Also add header propagation normalization.

ashley: Console work: add a small control panel to set sampling % per route and see immediate effect via `trace.sample_rate` metric. Can we surface estimate of extra storage cost when increasing sample %?

maria: Yes — Redwood Optimize should provide a rough delta: estimated traces/day * avg span size => bytes. Product wants that before enabling >5% sampling.

oliver: One more thing: asynchronous tasks spawned after HTTP response need to carry the `x-rw-req-id` and `parent_span` to be linkable. We'll patch task queue lib to auto-inject.

ben: Security note: don't leak user PII in trace annotations. Sampled traces must be scrubbed by default. Add a redact hook for common fields.

sam_oncall: TL;DR action items: @kevin runtime PR for header normalization and sampling API; @oliver task-queue patch; @ashley console panel + cost estimate; @ben redact hook + trace exporter throttling; @maria wire up dashboard queries and alert rules.

kevin: I'll open the PR tonight and add unit tests for header acceptance and `x-rw-force-sample` handling.

maria: Great — please post PR link here and set reviewers: eng-runtime, eng-infra, obs. We can sync in tomorrow's eng-platform standup if needed. :thumbsup:
